verdict.i_detail: After propagating loa-0 calibration Poisson noise, corrected by_snr chi2/dof 3.6/5.9/4.9 < corrected window by_nhat 9.4/9.7/8.9: the N-hat axis remains the leading residual. by_snr was the arm MOST inflated by unpropagated calibration noise (var ratios 5.5-17.4x).
verdict.ii_origin: MIXTURE: ~85-95% of the survey-only by_snr chi2 is calibration sampling noise. The survivor (joint p 0.002-0.02, max|z|<=4) is SIGNAL-SIDE SNR dependence (no-FP fold under-predicts [2,3) by 17-19%, over-predicts [7,inf) by 3.3-3.8%). Not FP SNR misallocation (tested direction worsens 3-4x), not truth stratification (<=1.4%), not a support hole. Candidates: per-stratum completeness error, kernel SNR dependence, unmodelled sub-19.0 promotions at low SNR (one-sided-support class).
verdict.iii_model_freedom: NOT justified. Correct fix: propagate calibration uncertainty in the gate statistics (delta variance or the b1 null). The full model already samples lam_fp; only the selftest/gate plugs the raw point estimate into a survey-only z.
verdict.iv_closure_and_fp_repair: Closure-failure verdict STANDS (window by_nhat 8.9-9.7 corrected, >= 3x the ratified gate). The FP-repair overshoot -1.80/-3.45/-2.61% is largely within the template's own calibration noise (full-total z -> -0.09/-2.77/-1.54; fp_w*sqrt(89) ~ 1565 counts ~ 1.8% of total); marginal only on London-0 (~-2.8 sigma), and the three mocks share the same 89-event draw so this is one observation, not three.
